grades.quote: The contents of the TLB are invalidated according to the information of the TLB-related CSRs to maintain the consistency of the page table data between the TLB and the memory.
grades.reason: Describes a LoongArch TLB-maintenance instruction that invalidates TLB entries to keep the TLB consistent with the page table in memory. It gives the invalidation mechanism, but it doesn't explicitly tie it to software changing a page table, and it is only one of the TLB invalidation instructions.
This is pseudocode for the TLB lookup (hit selection in the STLB and MTLB). It says nothing about invalidating stale translations or keeping them consistent after page table changes.

grades.quote: To ensure that implicit reads observe writes to the same memory locations, an SFENCE.VMA instruction must be executed after the writes to flush the relevant cached translations.
grades.reason: States directly that software must execute SFENCE.VMA after writes to the translation data structures to flush the relevant cached translations. It also explains how the address-translation cache can hold stale entries.

grades.quote: Synchronizing the hart’s address-translation caches with other forms of updates to a memory-resident PTE, including when a PTE is changed from Valid to Invalid, requires the use of suitable memory-management instructions.
grades.reason: Covers the RISC-V rule for synchronizing address-translation caches after PTE updates. Svvptc makes SFENCE.VMA unnecessary when a PTE goes from Invalid to Valid, but other updates, such as Valid to Invalid, still need memory-management instructions. This is useful but covers only part of the topic.
